inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (FYE 2026-01-30) cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation $247M. Lowe's publishes no separate equity-award tax-withholding line (us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation untagged since 2013); withheld shares sit inside repurchases, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = cash-flow add-back. Immaterial either way at 0.29% of revenue.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Friday nearest 31 January (52/53-week). FY0 is the year ended 2026-01-30, which Metrics.csv labels FY2026 and Lowe's itself calls fiscal 2025. Year 1 of the model is Lowe's fiscal 2026 (ends ~2027-01-29), the year management guided in August 2026.
inputs.share_count_basis: 561.0M = cover-page shares outstanding at 2026-08-25 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding 561.05M); diluted weighted-average for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 was 560.4M, basic 559.1M, so the dilutive overhang is ~1M shares. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and buybacks (which kept the count falling 1,473M -> 561M over 18 years) are value-neutral in this model. FY2026 buybacks were paused to delever after FBM; the flat count is therefore a modelling convention the company is currently funding only to the extent of SBC-offset repurchases ($366M in H1 FY2026).
inputs.net_debt_basis: Balance sheet at 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2026 10-Q): long-term debt incl. current maturities and finance leases 37,556 (35,204 non-current + 2,352 current, us-gaap:LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations*) less cash 3,172 = net debt 34,384. Short-term investments of 235 are excluded (largely restricted collateral for the extended-protection-plan program). Operating lease liabilities of 4,467 (733 current + 3,734 non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt because operating lease cost ($768M FY2025) is expensed inside EBITDA under ASC 842 -- treatment (B). Finance leases (~$390M) are inside the 37,556 and their ROU amortisation is inside D&A, which is consistent for that small piece. NOTE: Metrics.csv's FY2026 TotalDebt of 42,250 double-counts the current portion (LongTermDebt 39,819 + current 2,431); the correct 2026-01-30 figure is 39,921. Flagged for make fix; not used here.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.05 -> cost of equity 9.45%. Pre-tax cost of debt 4.8% (FY2025 interest expense $1,512M on ~$37B average debt = 4.1%, with the Sept-2025 FBM notes priced ~5%), after-tax 3.65% at 24%. Market-value weights E 73% ($102B at the quoted price) / D 27% ($37.6B) -> 7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality and integration risk are charged ONCE, in the scenario flows, weights and terminal caps, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. ASC 842 operating lease expense (FY2025 OperatingLeaseCost $768M, variable lease cost $305M) is inside EBITDA and cash rent is inside OCF, so no lease_cost_pct_path is needed and operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. D&A used for cash-tax EBIT is the cash-flow-statement DD&A (2,194), which contains finance-lease ROU amortisation (82) but NOT operating-lease ROU amortisation (572, which is part of rent expense), so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Lowe's has no non-controlling interests; all subsidiaries (incl. ADG and FBM) are wholly owned.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical consumer', owner-fcf.md plus the cyclical/lease adaptations). Lowe's is a US home-improvement retailer whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no other routing row applies. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). NEGATIVE BOOK EQUITY: shareholders' equity is -$7.4B at 2026-07-31 after ~$80B of cumulative buybacks; this is a capital-structure artefact (book), not a solvency signal -- EV/EBITDA, net debt/EBITDA (~2.7x on FY2025 EBITDA 12,347 vs 34.4B net debt) and interest cover (~6.7x) are the relevant tests, and any P/B or equity-CAGR sanity check is undefined for this name. The DCF is built on enterprise value and bridges to equity through net debt only; nothing in the valuation depends on book equity. ACQUISITIONS: ADG ($1.3B, Jun-2025) and FBM ($8.8B, Oct-2025) are inside FY0 revenue only part-year (~$2.3B of a combined ~$7B annual run-rate), so year-1 growth of 6.6% is mostly roll-in on roughly flat comps (guidance ~$92B sales, flat comps, adj. operating margin ~11.6%, adj. EPS ~$12.25, capex ~$2.5B, all set at the bottom of the prior range in Aug-2026). Capital returns: buybacks paused to repay the FBM term debt ($2.4B repaid in H1 FY2026, net debt down ~$4.2B from Jan-2026); dividend $2.6B/yr continues. Interest income (FY2025 $121M on the briefly held pre-FBM cash pile) is below EBITDA and is NOT in the flows, so nothing is double-counted against the cash deducted in the bridge.
inputs.price_volatility_note: Regular-session close; not an after-hours print. Price sits ~2% above the 52-week low after a ~38% drawdown from the 52-week high.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment anchored on the 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2016->FY2026 rows, 59,074 -> 86,286 = 3.9%/yr) and on FY2026 guidance for year 1; the equity CAGR is undefined (book equity has been negative since FY2022) and the 3y/5y revenue CAGRs are distorted by the pandemic peak (FY2022-FY2023 rows at $96-97B) and the 2023 sale of Lowe's Canada.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is undefined (negative book equity from buybacks), so the primary selection rule cannot be applied. Revenue CAGRs over 3y/5y are negative (post-pandemic normalisation plus the Canada divestiture) while EPS CAGRs are +5% to +9% -- the entire gap is share count (750M -> 561M) and margin, not organic growth. Owner-FCF CAGR (4.2% 3y, -4.1% 5y) tracks reported FCF closely because SBC is only ~0.3% of revenue; SBC is not eating cash-flow growth here.
historical_growth.notes: FY rows are Metrics.csv labels (FY2026 = year ended 2026-01-30). Owner-FCF series used for the FCF CAGRs: FY2021 9,103; FY2023 6,536; FY2026 7,404 (reported FCF less SBC; no interest-income strip since the company is net-debt throughout).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 6.6% = guided ~$92B on FY0 86,286: FBM/ADG full-year roll-in (~$4.7B incremental) on flat comps. Y2-5 3.5% = 2-3% comps as housing turnover normalises off a 30-year low, plus ~1pt from Pro/distribution share gains. Fades to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 14.0% EBITDA = guided 11.6% adj. operating margin + ~2.4% D&A ex acquired-intangible amortisation, less ~30bp FBM mix dilution. Rises 80bp over the decade from FBM/ADG synergies, Pro mix and PPI productivity to 14.8% -- inside the FY2022-FY2025 range (14.3%-15.6%), below Home Depot's ~16%.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 2.7% Y1 (guided ~$2.5B) easing to 2.5% (10-year average 2.0-2.3% plus distribution-branch growth). D&A 2.8% Y1 (H1 FY2026 DD&A 1,292 annualised incl. ~$400M acquired-intangible amortisation) fading to 2.6% as intangibles amortise.
base.wc_rationale: Net working capital (inventory 17,737 + receivables 1,238 - payables 11,076 = 7,899 at 2026-07-31) is ~9% of revenue; incremental capture set at -6% of the revenue change (growth consumes cash) net of deferred-revenue and accrued-liability offsets.
base.tax_rationale: 24% cash rate on EBIT = 21% federal + ~3% state, matching the FY2025 effective rate (~24%) and FY2025 cash taxes paid of 2,505 on ~$8.75B pre-tax. No NOLs or credits to ramp.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8%/2.5% implies 18.6x terminal FCF; capped at 16x -- below the 20x house default because home improvement is housing-cycle-exposed, but above the 12-15x cyclical band because this is a scaled duopoly franchise that has compounded through cycles. Today's EV/owner-FCF is ~18.5x, so the model does NOT assume multiple expansion.

bull.rationale: Housing cycle turns in 2027 (rate cuts lift existing-home turnover and remodel spend: comps +4-5% for three years), FBM/ADG cross-sell lifts Pro penetration toward 35%, synergies and Pro mix take EBITDA margin to 15.8% (approaching Home Depot). Exit multiple 18x reflects a market that again prices Lowe's as a through-cycle compounder; same 8% WACC.

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands at the guided floor, then a 2027 consumer/housing recession takes comps -4% to -5% (revenue -2% on acquisition roll-in), DIY-heavy mix deleverages EBITDA margin to 12.5% (the FY2023-row trough, ex-impairment, was ~14%; FY2009-FY2011 operating margins were 6-7%, so 12.5% is a moderate, not a worst-case, trough), FBM integration disappoints and distribution margins dilute the recovery to 13.3%. Exit multiple 13x -- the cyclical band -- as the market prices Lowe's as a levered housing cyclical. Same 8% WACC; the risk is in the flows.

scenario_narratives.base: Lowe's fiscal 2026 lands on the guided numbers -- ~$92B sales (flat comps plus the FBM/ADG roll-in), ~11.6% adjusted operating margin, ~$2.5B capex -- and the next four years deliver 3.5% growth as housing turnover grinds back from a 30-year low and Pro/distribution gains ~1pt of share a year. EBITDA margin climbs 80bp over the decade as FBM synergies, Pro mix and productivity offset lower-margin distribution revenue. Free cash flow first repays the FBM term debt, then resumes buybacks; the model treats those buybacks as value-neutral and credits the cash through the net-debt bridge. The axes are (1) housing turnover / mortgage rates, (2) Pro penetration vs Home Depot, (3) FBM/ADG integration, and (4) DIY discretionary mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate cuts in 2027 unlock the locked-in-mortgage housing market; existing-home sales and remodel spend recover for three years (comps +4-5%). FBM and ADG give Lowe's a credible large-Pro and new-construction channel, cross-sell works, and Pro penetration moves toward 35%. Margins reach 15.8% on synergies and mix, approaching Home Depot's level, and the market re-rates the stock back to an 18x FCF exit as a through-cycle compounder. This needs two independent things -- a macro housing recovery and acquisition execution -- which is why its weight is below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: The DIY shopper management already calls 'wary' retrenches further into a 2027 housing/consumer recession; comps fall 4-5% and the DIY-heavy, discretionary mix deleverages EBITDA margin to 12.5%. FBM, bought at the top with $8.8B of debt, under-delivers and its lower-margin distribution revenue caps the recovery at 13.3%. With net debt/EBITDA pushing 3x and negative book equity, buybacks stay suspended and the market prices Lowe's as a levered housing cyclical at a 13x FCF exit. Tariffs on the ~20% China-sourced mix add a persistent cost headwind. Solvency is not in question -- interest cover stays above 4x even here -- but equity value compresses hard.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: FY2026 guidance was cut to the floor of the range in August, mortgage rates hit a one-year high in September, the DIY mix is the most housing-sensitive in the category, and the FBM debt (net debt/EBITDA ~2.7x) removes the buyback cushion that has historically absorbed down-cycles. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires two independent events -- a rate-driven housing recovery AND successful integration/cross-sell of two large acquisitions -- to go right together. Base 50%: the guided year is credible and the long-run 3.5% growth / 14.8% margin path is squarely inside Lowe's own ten-year history.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Lowe's is valued as a stream of unlevered owner free cash flow discounted at an 8% USD WACC, with the equity found by subtracting $34.4B of net debt -- book equity is negative and irrelevant. SBC is tiny (0.3% of revenue) and fully expensed, so house and street values nearly coincide and the valuation turns almost entirely on four judgments: the pace of a housing-turnover recovery, how far FBM/ADG lift Pro penetration and margin, the exit multiple a cyclical retailer deserves (16x base, 13x-18x across scenarios, versus ~18.5x today), and the probability weights. The 10-year horizon lets margins mature before the terminal value is capitalised, and the terminal cap, not Gordon, binds in every scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Housing turnover and mortgage rates: comps are the single largest swing factor; a 2027 recession (bear) versus a 2027 recovery (bull) is worth roughly 2x in equity value because leverage magnifies EV changes
Terminal multiple: with ~55-60% of EV in the terminal value and net debt of $34B, each 1x of terminal FCF multiple moves equity value by roughly $9/share
FBM/ADG integration and distribution-margin dilution: $10.1B of 2025 M&A at a cyclical peak must earn its cost of capital for the base margin path to hold
Leverage: net debt/EBITDA ~2.7x with buybacks paused; the flat share count assumes repurchases resume once the term debt is repaid
Tariffs on ~20% China-sourced merchandise and commodity (lumber, gypsum) swings
Competitive share loss to Home Depot in Pro, where Lowe's is structurally underweight
